function: MAPPO agents jointly choose RIS phase-shift matrices and RIS deployment location (BS agents) and the edge server of each vehicle (VUE agents) to maximize throughput, p. 6.
system: Multi-RIS VEC network: 4 BSs with 8 antennas, 4 passive reflecting RISs of 16 elements, 12 single-antenna VUEs; carrier frequency not stated, pp. 3-4 and 9.
method: Multi-agent PPO (MAPPO), centralized training with decentralized execution, hybrid continuous-discrete actions, two agent types (BS-ES and VUE), parameter sharing; reinforcement learning, trained in simulation, pp. 6-8.
data_channel: Own Python simulator: block-fading Rician/Rayleigh channels with LoS BS-RIS link, path-loss exponents 2.2, 2.1 and 4.6, perfect CSI at BSs; no dataset, pp. 8-9.
test_conditions: Trained and scored in the same simulated environment by cumulative reward; Figs. 10-12 show separate convergence curves for varying RIS elements, VUE number and VUE power, p. 12.
baselines: Learned: MADDPG and MATD3; MAPPO without RIS and without service migration (ablations). No classical or non-learned method: the paper judges that comparison infeasible, pp. 11-12.
metrics: Accumulated reward (weighted sum throughput with delay penalty) versus iterations and running time; sum-throughput gain 26.41% over no RIS and 23.65% over no migration, pp. 9-12.
complexity: Per-episode MAPPO complexity O(sum over agents of 2T(Z+1) times layer-size products) plus O((I+K)^2 F T) for GAE, p. 8; convergence versus running time, p. 11.
q1_support: p. 9: "In this paper, Rician fading channel model is adopted"; BS-VUE and RIS-VUE links are Rayleigh and the path-loss exponents 2.2, 2.1 and 4.6 are set by the authors. No 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "Convergence performance of MAPPO-based algorithm with varying number of VUEs". Figs. 10-12 are convergence curves of each setting, so each condition has its own training; no trained policy is tested in an unseen scenario and no fine-tuning or transfer is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "it is difficult to carry out the work of comparing the proposed algorithm with the classical algorithms". Only MADDPG and MATD3 (learned) are compared; the no-RIS and no-migration schemes still run MAPPO, so they are ablations, not non-learned baselines.
q4_support: p. 8: "The complexity of DRL algorithms mainly comes from the forward propagation of the action prediction process"; Section III-C then gives the per-episode order O(...) for all agents.
q5_support: p. 8: "the simulation is implemented in Python 3.8 with PyTorch toolbox". No code or data link and no public dataset: the channels are generated by the authors' own simulator (p. 9).
notes: Included: the BS agents learn the RIS phase-shift matrices (area 3) together with the RIS deployment location, and the VUE agents choose the edge server (above PHY); a physical-layer decision learned jointly with one above it passes above_phy (p. 6: "The BSs with integrated ESs play the role of agents to control the deployment of RISs"; p. 13: "jointly optimizing computational ESs for the VUEs, the deployment locations and reflection matrices of the RISs"). The receive beamformer is closed-form, not learned (p. 4). Tables II and III (p. 9) are images, read from the PDF. Figs. 3 to 12 show convergence of the accumulated reward.
